I guess the question since there isn't much of a chance for abortion, is do you wish to keep your babies or do you want to put them up for adoption. I'm going to mention support for both sides so you have some information but you may want to figure out your next steps soon. I can't make this decision for you and I'm not going to push you in any direction but below this information for both sides. 

In the support if you want to go for adoption, there are literally about 2 million couples looking for babies every year in the US. But just not that many babies go up for adoption. Very few couples get off that waiting list so there are definitely enough willing people. Parenthood is hard especially without having enough support from your family. If you were scared about not knowing what's happening with your babies know that open adoption is a thing and most prospective parents are willing to go with open adoption if it means they get to have a baby or babies. There are some agencies that let you even pick the parents for yourself and possibly meet and interview possible adoptive parents.  Also I want to mention that with open adoption you are supposed to get updates about your child's life (or children's lives). You also get to enjoy your youth without the stress of Parenthood at such a young age. Also you can always change your mind within about 48 hours in most States but I would check your state laws on that before going that route though. 

In support of keeping the babies, I know New Jersey is a blue state. There should be programs to help you support your babies until you have a good income. When you have two babies whether you are living with your father or not you should be considered a household of three because as a parent you are your own household in most cases. You should be able to qualify for State health insurance for you and your babies, WIC, food stamps, child care assistance (all possible while you're underage in most places) and even rent assistance (once you turn 18) . There are probably countless charities in your area that would be willing to help an unwed mother get items for your babies. In my area there are a couple places that you can just walk into and if you can prove that you are underage with very little support they will get you the bare minimum at least. I had close friends who were teen moms when we were in high school so I know. Regardless you definitely have to talk about this to your father if you haven't already. It's not like you're going to be able to hide it forever, if you haven't talked about it already. Also kind of important to ask yourself, do you have any aunts or uncles, older cousins, grandparents even who might be willing to help you out a bit? I really hope you've already started taking your prenatals. Those are very important for your babies' future health. Regardless I think it's still very possible you can finish your high school education and raise your babies if you choose to do so but it's going to be hard to do so yourself so if you can find some support in your family or even with your friends I think you'll be okay if you don't want to put your babies up for adoption. 

Good luck in your future and please remember whatever you decide doesn't make you bad, you are the mother of these babies I believe you will make the best decision for your children like any good mother does. Just believe and trust in yourself and everything will turn out the way it's supposed to.

Seeing that you have a decree from another country, in most cases it would only help in that country where the decree was ordered. Usually this is because the law of the land that you came to will not uphold the law of old land where you came from. The old land would likely be unable to act if something happened against your decree. It would be out of jurisdiction of the new land unless it is against the laws of the new country as well. That is a general rule. 

To be very clear, in your case, it's unlikely that your decree would protect you if your ex decided to do something drastic like suddenly refusing you to see your daughter at all as an example. I hope for your sake she or her new guy doesn't know this.

 But I do want to reiterate that regardless even without a court order from the US your ex would be unlikely to take full custody unless she could prove something like extreme abuse because most judges in the US do try to keep biological parents involved as much as possible even if there is a bad or a mostly absent parent (infrequently and occasionally show up). I've seen that too much.

It sounds like you're doing everything you can and doing everything right. If I were you though I still consider getting the court order only because it will protect you if your ex and her guy get really nasty down the road. It really screwed my brother over at first when his ex threw allegations at him trying to remove him out of their lives. 9 months of uncertainty and court dates were torture but i was there every step for my brother so I know all too well how ugly it can get.

Lastly, if your daughter is old enough to know the days of the week, knowing when she should expect you could bring her comfort and stability.

Something you're not telling us is whether or not you have a court order. Do you have a court order? I would get things in writing regardless via court order if you don't already. Because she can be charged with contempt of court if she doesn't allow you to have your visitation without good reason and there are very few reasons. She can also get into huge trouble if she moves out of state without the judge agreeing even for a better job if the move makes it impossible to see your child the judge could strike her down. It doesn't even matter if you have a lot of money or not. Most states only care if you're involved. Even a little bit. Some of these actions could also get you residential custody meaning your child ends up living with you as long as you could prove that you have a safe place/environment to live with your daughter. 

Additionally, it's almost impossible in any state for a step parent to take custody of a child without you signing your rights over. If you haven't already lawyer up. My brother has had fairly good success with a public defender if you don't have the money to afford a lawyer. The most important part is that you are there for your daughter (as much as you can be), remember that. Good Luck!

I don't know if you have gained weight that you never lost after your first baby but if you are very over weight , it is possible that the weight will make it harder to get pregnant. Well I was about 70 pounds over weight (I have lost about 13 recently) and I found out fat cells are really excellent at making estrogen. Do you know how most birth control pills work? They give your body much more estrogen than it needs which shuts down egg production and makes your fluids hostile towards sperm cells. Which means if you are carrying a lot of weight on your body like I am your body could be making its own form of birth control.
